subject: multi-provider-gateway-plane
seam: Error::is_router_failure() beside is_terminal_for_job in crates/core/src/error.rs, read in exactly one place — trace_tier_error in crates/core/src/fetcher.rs, which every tier's error arm already funnels through — so the fetch ladder gains the technique's second break arm; fixture crates/core/tests/router_versus_candidate.rs
seam_notes: Measured A/B in-tree by disabling the break arm and re-running the fixture. Arm A: a router-caused failure at the http tier walked http, browser and claude and returned 'app: all fetch tiers exhausted for … (attempted: http, browser, claude)' — 3 engine invocations per failure. Arm B: 1 invocation and the error reaches the caller as itself ('config: missing [claude] api key'), which also gives the operator's row its origin for free with no worker.rs change. The un-skip at fetcher.rs:752 is the same fix and the same line: arm A logged 'http tier un-skipped: browser engine failed' on a config error and spent the tier the router had correctly skipped; arm B leaves the skip standing (http invoked 0 times) while an Error::Browser still un-skips it — the paired assertion. One carrier: the predicate on the existing typed enum, no header, no sentinel message, no second flag; the source's defect is two mechanisms (in-band marker plus a RouterError that escapes the loop and renders as a 400). Orthogonality preserved: is_terminal_for_job untouched, and the predicate is an exhaustive match with no wildcard, so the default is theirs and a new variant stops the build until someone decides. Gate: cargo check -p pumper-core green; cargo test -p pumper-core 3/3 new and 446+ existing green; cargo clippy -p pumper-core --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo check --workspace --all-targets green.
falsifier: The proposal's own falsifier fires and the direction understated it: a static census, not a jobs-table query (no retained DB in the worktree), finds NO producer of an ours-error on the ladder path today. Error::Config is minted only by Config::load/validate and Catalog::load (boot-time; validate() closes 29 cases before the server starts) and by no engine crate; Error::Transact comes from Browser::transact, which the ladder never calls; Error::ReplayMiss is raised at the AppContext chokepoint above the ladder; plugin errors never reach a fetch tier. So the amplification is real and now closed, but currently unreachable in production — the break arm is a guard, not a repair. Return condition: the first engine that types a misconfiguration as Error::Config at call time (the remote fabric and the archive engine are the likely first), or the first failed job row carrying 'config:' or 'plugin:' from a fetch tier. Also unfixed by design: the measurable the study stated as 'tiers × max_attempts → 1' cannot be reached by this context, which is forbidden from touching is_terminal_for_job — the max_attempts factor lives on that axis and Error::Config stays retryable at the job level. What moved is tiers → 1 per attempt.

technique: lease-renewal (absent is not lost; teardown is a held state)
subject: job-coordination
seam: crates/core/migrations/0017_job_heartbeat.sql; crates/server/src/worker.rs:861 heartbeat tick; crates/core/src/storage.rs:1015 heartbeat (attempt-fenced UPDATE), :1036 reap_stale, :439 complete; worker.rs:2745 a_reclaimed_attempt_does_not_fan_out
seam_notes: The lease is a column on the job row and every write is attempt-fenced, so a renewal that updates zero rows has one meaning (the attempt is over): re-establish-on-absent has no branch to take (the row is the lease), a vanished row is correctly fail-closed (the row is the work), and the store-flush eviction shape cannot occur (losing the store loses the jobs with the leases). Condition written into the amendment's closing paragraph. Separate structural fact against the BASE technique: worker.rs:861 discards the heartbeat's boolean, so a reaped task keeps working until its fenced completion is refused; the two-way channel (read the result, stop the loop) is the few-line change owed.
return_condition: When the lease moves to a store separate from the jobs table (shared Redis, a second instance); meanwhile: read the heartbeat result at worker.rs:861 and stop the task on false.

technique: guard-key-design (with the fence inside the claim's write transaction)
subject: concurrency-guards
seam: crates/core/src/storage.rs:38 TARGET_EXCLUSION + :464 claim_next (the clause lives inside the one atomic UPDATE ... WHERE id = (SELECT ...) RETURNING); crates/core/src/app.rs:955 ScrapeApp::target_key default None; crates/core/migrations/0041_job_target_key.sql; crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs:650 target_key_for (the one door helper, sibling of validate_app_params) called from all six enqueue doors; fixture crates/server/src/e2e/target_exclusion.rs
seam_notes: Measured A/B in-tree by blanking TARGET_EXCLUSION and re-running the fixture, which drives the two doors that legitimately skip dedup (the cron fire path through scheduler::reconcile and POST /apps/{name}/jobs with no idempotency key) and the REAL worker loop with concurrency 4 and no per-app cap. Arm A: peak concurrent runs against one target_key = 2, and the two rows' started_at/finished_at windows overlap. Arm B: 1, and the windows are disjoint. The paired assertions are what keep the fix from being the per-app cap in disguise and both PASS in arm A too: two jobs of the same app with DIFFERENT target keys still peak at 2, and two jobs with a NULL key peak at 2 (an app that has not overridden target_key is not serialised against every other). The guard is in the claim's SELECT rather than in the worker on purpose: no window between check and claim, and a second pumper process would inherit it while inheriting nothing from a worker-side list. Non-starvation is the existing notify_one on every finish. Operator half: pumper_jobs_held_by_target on /metrics, counted with the claim's own predicate negated so the gauge cannot drift from the guard, which splits 'queued and due' into behind (a capacity finding) and held (not one). Two apps override target_key - grants-gov and ca-grants, each of which upserts one whole opportunities dataset per run with its pagination internal to the job, so an overlap is never throughput. Gate on branch direction/kube-rs-round5: cargo test -p pumper-core / -p pumper-server / -p app-grants-gov / -p app-ca-grants green (4 new e2e cases), cargo clippy --workspace --tests clean, cargo fmt --check clean.
falsifier: The direction's own pre-acceptance number was NOT taken: there is no retained jobs history in the worktree, so the base rate of same-app same-source overlap is unmeasured and this ships as a guard rather than a repair. Return condition: one observed double-write (a dataset row whose provenance shows two job ids at the same instant), or the overlap query over a real store. Also unbuilt: the schedule-health vocabulary that would render a held job as 'held' rather than 'late' in GET /schedules - the job row carries target_key and the gauge carries the count, so the derivation is one step away and was left out rather than half-built.

subject: convergence-loop-and-requeue
seam: crates/core/src/storage.rs:150 requeue_after(error, attempts, stated) -> Requeue (pure, now-free) + :100 ladder_delay + :55 FailReason (Typed|Text) + :690 Storage::fail; crates/engine-http/src/lib.rs:950 budget_exhausted carries the stated wait it could not honour; crates/core/src/error.rs Error::http_after/stated_retry_after; crates/core/migrations/0042_job_requeue_reason.sql; fixture crates/server/src/e2e/requeue_policy.rs
seam_notes: Measured A/B in-tree by disabling the policy's two opinionated arms and re-running the fixture on the trait-level fake seam (a scripted HttpClient an app reaches through ctx.engines.http and propagates with ?, which is how every API-shaped app in crates/apps raises a transport failure). Arm A: an origin stating Retry-After 600 cost 3 engine invocations inside a one-minute observation window (the ladder placed retries at 10s and 20s, both inside it) and a config error burned 3 attempts. Arm B: 1 invocation with available_at at least 600s out, and 1 attempt. The harness fast-forwards only delays that fall INSIDE the window - a wait we are not allowed to shorten ends the loop instead of being simulated through, which is the whole point of the stated-wait arm. The control (an ordinary connection reset) rides all three attempts in both arms. Third number: a table test over one instance of every variant the policy has no opinion about asserts the default arm is byte-identical to 10*2^attempts capped at 3600; jitter stays a property of the write (job id + attempt seed), not of the policy, and only ever lengthens, so a stated wait is never shortened by the spread. The registry's rule that giving up must be visible is honoured by jobs.requeue_reason ('attempt ladder' | 'server-stated wait' | 'store contention' | 'ours-class failure'), without which this trades a predictable ladder for a smarter opaque one. One carrier: the retry_after field on Error::Http, minted at the single site that learns and abandons a stated wait, never a sentinel in the message. Gate on branch direction/kube-rs-round5: cargo test --workspace green (6 new unit + 3 new e2e), cargo clippy --workspace --tests clean, cargo fmt --check clean.
falsifier: The carrier does NOT survive the tiered fetcher: fetcher.rs's ladder_exhausted flattens every tier failure into Error::App('all fetch tiers exhausted ...'), so a stated wait learned on the http tier is lost for apps that fetch through ctx.fetch, and the arm only fires for the eleven raw-HTTP apps that call ctx.engines.http directly (which are the API-shaped ones that actually meet 429s). Stated in the fixture and in the fetch-chokepoint inventory row rather than papered over. Also not taken: the direction's pre-acceptance base rate (share of failed rows carrying a 429/503-with-wait or a config:/plugin: prefix) - no retained history in the worktree.

subject: error-handling
seam: crates/core/src/error.rs:155 CauseValue (boxed cause + the type name captured at the raise site) + Error::{http,browser,parse,config}_from constructors + Error::cause()/cause_kind()/cause_chain(); crates/engine-http/src/lib.rs:887 transport_error (the one reqwest mapping, retryable arm keeps the reqwest::Error); crates/core/migrations/0043_job_cause_kind.sql; guard crates/core/tests/error_cause_chain.rs
seam_notes: Measured by an inventory guard in the EXPECTED-diff idiom expected_terminal already uses: sites in crates/core + crates/engine-http where one of the four cause-carrying constructors is handed a message built from a cause it does not keep ({e}, {e:?}, or e.to_string()) - 18 before, 3 after, each of the three pinned with its reason (scraper's SelectorErrorKind is !Send + !Sync + !'static, so it cannot be boxed into a cause that crosses tokio::spawn). The guard was run against a deliberately reverted site to prove it fires (4 found, 3 allowed). Paired assertion: 22 sites DO attach a cause, so the guard cannot pass by nobody raising these variants any more. Display is untouched and every message still interpolates its cause, so no job row's text moved - what is added is the value beside the sentence. Consumer proofs: a real refused connection (127.0.0.1:1) classifies through the cause with is_connect()/is_timeout()/is_decode() and NO string in the assertion; a failed job row records cause_kind = 'toml::de::error::Error' while a text-only failure records NULL; GET /jobs/{id}/receipt renders cause_kind and requeue_reason beside the sentence. The boundary is stated in the module docs: is_terminal_for_job and is_router_failure still match on the variant, exhaustively, and must never consult a source. Gate on branch direction/kube-rs-round5: cargo test --workspace green (4 new guard/round-trip cases + 1 engine-http case), cargo clippy --workspace --tests clean, cargo fmt --check clean.
falsifier: Two honest deviations. (1) The direction's headline '186 sites' is a workspace-wide count across all fourteen String variants; re-measured for the four variants with the guard's own rule it is 18 in the two governed crates (30 across all of crates/), and crates/apps constructs none of the four at all. The remaining ~11 sites outside the governed crates are deliberately NOT pinned - the pattern spreads into them, and pinning the workspace would turn a landing into a rewrite. (2) The chain is exposed as Error::cause()/cause_chain() rather than through std::error::Error::source, because thiserror's #[source] cannot take an Option<Box<dyn Error>> and a non-optional wrapper would make every causeless failure report a source that renders as nothing. A generic error-chain walker therefore still sees nothing under these variants. Return condition: thiserror gaining optional source fields, at which point the derive replaces the accessor.

subject: untrusted-extension-host
seam: crates/engine-wasm/src/lib.rs:571-596 (StoreLimits: memory/memories/tables/table_elements/instances caps, set_fuel, instantiation refusal classed as Trap) and :848-853 (a fuel/memory trap during the call is PluginFailure::Trap); crates/server/src/triggers.rs:190-195 (the host decides the direction of a trapped predicate: fail-open unless on_error=skip); lib.rs:4-5 (plugins have no imports)
seam_notes: Three real cases walked under A (publish one word, sandboxed) and B (publish counted vs uncounted ceiling lists): (1) a runaway plugin burns its fuel and traps - uncatchable by the guest, classed Trap, direction chosen by the host per hook class (e2e a_real_trap_leaves_a_hook_trap_row_while_the_hop_still_fires, trigger_plugins.rs:520); (2) a fuel burn under on_error=skip stops the hop without faking a veto (:558); (3) a module whose declared memory exceeds the cap is refused at instantiation, also classed Trap (lib.rs:590-596). Under both arms every case ends the same way, because the counted list (fuel, linear memory, tables, instances) is already published in GET /plugins telemetry (fuel_budget, memory_bytes_cap; lib.rs:102-112) and the uncounted list is empty by construction: the plugins import nothing, so there is no host call in which wall time or host-side allocation could escape the count. The amendment rule the tree confirms structurally is its third one - the uncounted list is empty exactly when the guest imports nothing.
falsifier: the first host import added to the linker (a fetch, a log) makes the uncounted list non-empty; at that moment the telemetry must grow a second list (wall-time bound at the call boundary, host-side allocation limiter) or the word sandboxed becomes the over-claim the amendment warns about. Instrument: the count of imports in the Linker, currently zero; and whether GET /plugins says so.

subject: test-input-generation
seam: crates/server/src/e2e/trigger_plugins.rs (the only harness that drives the real wasm host through the predicate -> transform -> record stages; every case is end to end) and crates/server/src/triggers.rs:302-306 (the masking the tree already met: a predicate that never loaded takes the same fail-open path as one that passed, so a gate nobody deployed is indistinguishable from a gate that said yes)
seam_notes: Three real cases under A (one end-to-end harness, as today) and B (one target per stage, triaged in pipeline order, the wasm stage under its fuel budget): (1) every_sandbox_failure_mode_fails_open_not_closed (trigger_plugins.rs:340): under A a predicate trap fires the hop open and the transform stage runs on an input the predicate never judged - a transform defect on that input is masked by the predicate failure; under B the predicate target drains its crash set first and the transform target is fed only inputs the predicate stage accepted, so the transform defect is reachable. (2) non_json_transform_output_is_recorded_as_malformed (:604): under A the malformed-output path is reached only through a full hop; under B it is the transform target own oracle (output must parse as JSON) and every generated envelope exercises it. (3) a_missing_plugin_is_recorded_once_not_once_per_event (:673): the tree own fix for stage masking - missing_hook_plugins reports the unrunnable stage at error level instead of letting it pass open silently - is the technique first decision rule (justify the middle stage in writing) already paid for once. Predicted: B finds transform defects that A cannot reach on inputs the predicate stage rejects or traps on; A finds only what survives the predicate.
falsifier: if no transform-stage defect exists behind a predicate failure in the e2e corpus, the extra target finds nothing and B costs a harness for no finding; measurable by running the transform target alone over the inputs the predicate stage trapped on and counting distinct failures. Return: build the per-stage harness as a task (predicate target + transform target over the wat fixtures already in trigger_plugins.rs), sized ~2 files / ~150 lines, gate: cargo test -p pumper-server e2e.

subject: self-healing
seam: crates/server/src/worker.rs:815-831 (catch_unwind around app.run(ctx), with the source comment that enumerates what it CANNOT catch: a non-yielding wedge, and a hard abort via process::exit/OOM/SIGKILL - for both the reaper is the backstop and can only report "lease expired (heartbeat stale)") and crates/server/src/worker.rs:790-812 (AppContext, which carries spent_usd: Arc<SpentTotal>, the progress reporter, the checkpointer and the research cache across the would-be process boundary)
arms: A = today, work item as an in-process async task with unwind caught. B = the technique, one child process per work item, parent classifies from the child. Three real failure classes from the tree own comment: (1) panic -> equivalent, B buys nothing and costs a spawn; (2) non-yielding wedge -> B better, a true verdict instead of a stale-lease label; (3) hard abort -> B clearly better, only the child dies and sibling jobs on the same worker survive.
why_not_better: Two of three cases favour B and it still loses. The work item decrements a live shared spend counter (Arc<SpentTotal>, an AtomicU64) as it spends; that does not serialize into an invocation. Across a process boundary a child that spends and then hard-aborts in case 3 has consumed budget the parent never observed - reopening the record-precedes-effect window the fork was bought to close. In one address space the counter is updated before the spend call returns and the law holds for free.
structural_fact: The tree ALREADY forks one layer in: crates/engine-claude/src/lib.rs:155-159 spawns the model CLI as a child process. What crosses that boundary is a request and a response; what would cross the outer one is an accounting reference. Nobody wrote a policy saying "fork where the state is small" - the boundary landed where the mutable state stopped. This tree applies the technique and declines it, correctly, in one call stack.
return_condition: When the cost ledger becomes write-ahead - a store the work item appends to BEFORE spending. The shape is already half present: spend is restored from checkpoints and cost events are recorded. Once it exists the disqualifier dissolves and case 3 wins outright; re-run this A/B then.

subject: test-input-generation
seam: crates/server/src/e2e/trigger_hook_stages.rs (new; two targets) + one line in crates/server/src/e2e/mod.rs. Asserts against crates/server/src/triggers.rs:179-188 (the predicate_verdict grammar), :253-289 (host_owned_overrides / restamp_host_owned, the transform re-stamp), :337-364 (HookVerdict.incidents), and pumper_core::storage::TRIGGER_OUTCOMES. The existing end-to-end file crates/server/src/e2e/trigger_plugins.rs is untouched and remains the end-to-end contract.
seam_notes: One target per stage whose input type differs from its predecessor's, both driving the real WasmPluginHost at 200_000 fuel per call, so a looping module is a trap and a finding rather than a hang and wall time is bounded by construction (time-over-budget is counted as its own class, 0 today). No generated-input library was used because the tree declares none: no workspace manifest names proptest, quickcheck, arbitrary or bolero, and rand/arbitrary reach Cargo.lock only transitively (wasmtime's cranelift-control, zip), so either would have been a new direct dependency edge for one test file. The generator is deterministic SplitMix64 written in the file, and a failing case prints the generated envelope itself, not the seed. 300 cases per target. PREDICATE TARGET: envelope (external_trigger_obj built by the host itself, plus hand-mirrored dataset and terminal shapes, each carrying one adjacent mutation - wrong-typed depth, dropped work-scope keys, keys at the 200 cap, chain collapsed to a scalar) x 15 verdict shapes (bare booleans, {pass: bool}, wrong-typed pass, near-miss key, every other JSON value, non-JSON bytes, an immediate trap, a fuel burn) x on_error in {absent, skip, fire}. Its oracle is the stage's own and is the anti-pattern triggers.rs:302-306 already paid for by hand: an empty incident list may ONLY ever mean a real pass=true, a veto is exactly one predicate_veto row, and a gate that did not answer must leave a row that is NOT predicate_veto and must fire iff on_error != skip. Measured: vetoed=46, unanswered=191, discard_fraction=0.000, over_budget=0. TRANSFORM TARGET: each envelope labelled by whether the predicate stage would have produced nothing at all (an honest veto, or unanswered under on_error=skip). Oracle: host_owned_overrides(original, result) is empty (the re-stamp held), the envelope leaves the stage as a JSON object, and non-object or failed output keeps the ORIGINAL envelope with exactly one Transform-slot incident, never a record of what the sandbox proposed. Measured: 117 of 300 envelopes reached the transform stage behind a predicate that stopped the hop - a set no end-to-end case can reach - and 2 distinct failure classes were found there (hook_malformed, hook_trap). That moves the direction's measurable off its 0-by-construction. GATE actually run, on the branch direction/test-input-generation: cargo test -p pumper-server --bin pumper trigger_hook_stages -- --nocapture => 'test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 507 filtered out', exit code 0; cargo fmt --check clean. SIZE: the proposal said 2 files / ~150 lines; landed at 2 files (one new, one mod.rs line) and 508 lines, of which 346 are code. The two targets are ~165 of those; the remaining ~180 is per-file scaffolding - the Trigger/PluginHook builders, the wat fixtures, the temp-dir host - that trigger_plugins.rs pays for separately and that could not be shared without making a private helper module out of a sibling test file.
falsifier: The proposal's three, each now instrumented rather than argued. (1) 'No transform defect exists behind a predicate failure, so the target is a cost with no finding' - refuted for now: 2 distinct classes are reachable there. The standing guard is the assertion that the class list is non-empty; if a later generator change empties it, that is the signal to delete the transform target, not to weaken the assertion. (2) 'The stages cannot fail independently' - they can: the transform stage runs and records on 117/300 envelopes for which the predicate stage produced nothing. (3) 'The generated envelopes cannot reach the transform's real inputs, so the target tests the reject path and reports green' - discard_fraction is printed every run and asserted below 0.2 (0.000 today); a rise after a generator edit is a generator that got worse while the suite stayed green. Known blind spot, stated in the file: the dataset and terminal envelope shapes are hand-mirrored because dataset_trigger_obj and terminal_trigger_obj need a Job and a &[&Revision] the crawl archive supplies, so a field added to either builder will not appear here and this target will report green on the older shape. Deliberately not absorbed: fuzzing the plugin binaries themselves, the fetch tier, and the existing e2e cases.

technique: tool-schema-design (error channels: route by actor) + one-validation-door at the tool surface
subject: mcp-tools
seam: crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs tools_call - arguments dispatched to handlers without ever being checked against the inputSchema this server publishes for that tool
measurable: published tool-schema constraints enforced at the dispatch door, and what a caller gets for a violating argument
arm_a: typo key {"q":"x","srot":"newest"} accepted, isError=false, request reached the handler with the key silently dropped - a plausible wrong answer with no signal; query_dataset missing its required dataset also accepted
arm_b: both refused in-band (isError=true) with the violation named by JSON pointer and an instruction to re-read the schema; refused request never reaches the index; valid call unaffected
gate: cargo test -p pumper-server 506+9 passed 0 failed; cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean
note: The finding was narrower than first stated and the tree corrected it: handlers DO enforce some advertised constraints by hand (search refuses a bad sort enum and a blank q, in-band, and that already matched the corrected registry rule). What no handler enforced was additionalProperties and required. So the defect is not absent validation but validation that lives per handler, where the set checked drifts from the set published. The door now holds what a schema can express; handlers keep what it cannot.
return_condition: a tool whose inputSchema stops compiling (validation silently skips, warn-logged only), or a handler rule that duplicates a schema constraint now enforced twice
